titel: Passato Prossimo Memory: Che cosa hai fatto?
untertitel: A first look at the *passato prossimo* with *avere* (*ho mangiato, ho comprato, ho fatto, ho visto*) – build sentences, ask questions, play memory. Verbs with *essere* (*sono andato*) come later.
grammatik: Passato prossimo with avere: first look (io form)
ho mangiato, ho comprato, ho fatto, ho visto

grammatik.regel: First look: the *passato prossimo* talks about finished times: *ieri, ieri sera, sabato, lunedì*. Here you only meet the *io* form (*ho* + participle) of a few common verbs. The participle: -are verbs end in *-ato* (comprare → _ho comprato_), -ere verbs in *-uto* (avere → _ho avuto_, bere → _ho bevuto_), -ire verbs in *-ito* (dormire → _ho dormito_). Very common irregular participles: fare → _ho fatto_, vedere → _ho visto_, prendere → _ho preso_, scrivere → _ho scritto_. Question to one person: *Che cosa hai fatto sabato?* A bracketed word like (io) says who is speaking; you don't write it.

redemittel.p1: Che cosa _hai fatto_ il fine settimana?

soGehts: Cut pages 2 and 3 in half. Cut out the word cards on page 4 too.
On your own (page 2): Put the tiles in order and write four sentences in the *passato prossimo*. Change the blue verb to the *io* form (*ho* + participle).
In pairs (page 3): Ask: “Che cosa hai fatto …?” Your partner answers with their sentence. Write the answer.
Game (page 4): Play memory with the word cards.
Finally: Che cosa hai fatto il fine settimana? Tell your partner.

hinweise: Blue tile = infinitive. Change it to the *io* form of the past: cucinare → ho cucinato, vedere → ho visto.
The time (sabato, ieri sera) comes first in these sentences.
Questions: Che cosa hai fatto …? A tile in brackets, like (io) or (tu), says who: don't write it.

regeln: Cut out the 24 word cards and put them face down on the table.
A turns over two cards and reads them aloud.
Do they match (cucinare – ho cucinato)? Then A says a sentence: “Ieri ho cucinato la pasta.”
The sentence is right? A keeps the pair and plays again. No pair, or the sentence is wrong: turn the cards back, and now it is B's turn.
Who has the most pairs at the end?
